statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk of 22% sits in the watch band, below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is WATCH. The evidence-based danger window runs from the 12:30Z September employment report through 15:00Z, covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds within 16 points of a twice-confirmed 31,029.50 high but hourly extension stalls, while VIX, yields and crude all decay into the September payrolls print
body: NQ futures trade 31,021.00 (+260.50, +0.85%) on a delayed CME quote timed 09:16:52Z, inside an overnight range of 30,760.25-31,029.50 against a 30,760.50 prior close. An independent delayed feed read 31,013.75 (+253.25, +0.82%) at the same minute and confirms the identical 31,029.50 high, so the extreme is corroborated rather than single-sourced. The band is about 0.88% wide and price sits roughly 8-16 points below the high, which keeps price holding near the extreme as the one live Tail amplifier. That amplifier weakened over the past hour: the session high advanced only 3.75 points, from 31,025.75 to 31,029.50, against roughly 88 points of extension in the hour before. This hour is consolidation at the high rather than repeated extension after failed retracements, which is the structure Tail is meant to measure. Cross-asset evidence runs the other way and is now unambiguous. VIX is 15.97, down 2.56% from a 16.39 close, in a 15.89-16.24 band and near its session low. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.232% against a 5.238% prior close in a 5.223-5.262 range, well below Thursday's 5.345% print, the highest since 2002; the 2-year is 4.785% against 4.787% in a 4.775-4.804 band. Crude has given back the whole of Thursday's geopolitical spike: WTI is 89.01 (-4.15%) and Brent 99.04 (-3.20%), after Brent closed Thursday up 4.4% at 102.31 and WTI settled up 2.7% at 92.87 on reports of a third U.S. carrier heading to the region. The proximate driver of the reversal is a verified partial supply recovery rather than sentiment: Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline and resumed tanker loadings at Yanbu, and European gas fell with it, the Dutch benchmark down 2.77% to EUR 71.90/MWh. Equities higher with volatility, yields and energy all decaying is a benign unwind of risk premium, not the stress-driven one-way repricing that normally precedes mean-reversion failure. The macro backdrop stays genuinely difficult, which is why Stress remains in the high band while Tail does not follow. Fed commentary this week was hawkish, not dovish: Dallas Fed President Logan said rates need to rise by at least 50 basis points to curb sticky inflation and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said more hikes will be needed into 2027, while traders pared October hike odds and most still price at least one 25 basis-point increase by December. Friday's long-end retreat is therefore better read as a retracement from a 24-year-high overshoot than as a dovish repricing. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed in the eighth month of the conflict after Washington rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire proposal, and an additional carrier plus 10,000 personnel have been deployed to the Gulf, so the energy channel can reopen on a single headline. Semiconductor and megacap tone is supportive, with AI chip names bid in premarket trade after Micron's strong fiscal fourth quarter, and the S&P 500 closed 1 October at 7,670.36, up 0.3%. The dominant scheduled checkpoint is the September employment report at 12:30Z, followed by August Factory Orders at 14:00Z. Published payrolls estimates are unusually dispersed, spanning roughly 84,000 to 100,000, with the unemployment rate seen steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings near 0.2-0.3% month over month against a prior +162,000 headline. Forecast dispersion of that kind raises Stress and tempers Confidence; under this contract it does not raise Tail before the print, and the 7 August experience, where a large payrolls surprise did not produce a no-retracement path, argues directly against pre-positioning Tail for a hypothetical post-release chain. Tail therefore steps down one point to 22% to record the stalled extension, staying above the 20% floor only because price sits at the extreme into a Tier-1 release. Mode remains trend-up because the session path is still a one-sided advance off the overnight low with price at the high, even though the latest hour was flat and the amplifier set around it is decaying. The shared Finviz context file was collected on 29 September at 23:14:22Z, roughly 58 hours before this assessment and far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, and is marked partial. It was treated as stale and contributed nothing here; all evidence above comes from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail opened the window at 20% in the 09:00Z hour on 1 October, peaked at 24% during the 14:00Z hour as the long-end selloff intensified, then printed 20% for fourteen consecutive hours before stepping to 21% at 07:00Z and 23% at 08:00Z as the European-morning advance gained genuine directional efficiency. Stress rose from 75% to a 79% overnight peak, held 78-79% through the Asian session and eased to 76% at the end of the window; Confidence stayed between 87% and 89% throughout. The 08:00Z hour is the only slot in the window published as trend-up rather than mixed.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 22% through the European morning while the 30,760.25-31,029.50 band is assumed to keep containing price, steps to 23% in the hour before the release as depth thins and 24% in the 12:30Z release hour, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, pullbacks that fail and a long-end break back above the 5.345% peak; it is not an assertion that such a path has formed. Tail then eases through the afternoon as repricing is assumed to complete, reaching the 20% floor at the 20:00Z cash close. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% across the release and open, then decays to a 60% weekend floor that still carries the unresolved long-end yield and Gulf energy questions. CME equity index futures halt at 21:00Z, so the final twelve slots hold the 20% floor as a carried rather than observed assessment while Confidence steps down to 75%. The next live reference is the Sunday reopen near 22:00Z on 4 October, and the next scheduled checkpoints are the S&P Global services final and ISM Services on 5 October, both outside this horizon.
